newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end mixed on rolling, liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end mixed on rolling, liquidation.

text.p: Rolling of long positions by funds and liquidation prompted by delivery concerns pressured May CME pork belly futures while supporting back months. Hog futures ended unevenly lower as the market awaited the next move in cash hogs, traders said.

Pork bellies posted a very wide trading range during the day with August and February surging the 3.000 cents per lb daily limit and posting a new high in August before falling briefly for a new loss in July and an extended loss in May. Futures ended 0.075 lower to 1.225 higher with July up 0.425 at 92.025 cents. August set a new high early of 92.625.

Funds rolled out of May ahead of its spot position Thursday with long liquidaiton also evident on concern over deliveries. Talk circulated in the pit that the current large holder of deliverable stocks would deliver up to 200 contracts because there was no carrying charge built into the market, they said.
However, July did go from a 0.050 cent discount to May Tuesday to a 1.100 cent premium by the end of trading.
Some selling also developed reflecting the expected pickup in slaughter and continued private reports of weakness in cash product which offset the bullish out-of-town report.

Pork bellies surged early following the CME weekly out-of-town report which showed an unexpectedly large out-movement of 1.205 million lbs. Estimates had ranged from in 200,000 to out 200,000 lbs. But profit taking and commercial sellling on the increased talk of easier product prices clipped gains, traders said.

USDA quoted 14-16 lb cash bellies at $90 per cwt at noon, but traders continued to point to reports of product selling as low as $85. Demand for product has dwindled since late last week as high prices cut off both domestic and export demand, they said.

LIT division of First Options and E.D.&F. Man notably spread long July/short May. LFG continued to sell July while Smith Barney and Prudential Securities bought. Prudential Securities, Spike Trading and Cargill Investor Services bought August early before locals sold, pit sources said.

Hog futures moved into a narrow trading range as the market awaited the next move in cash hogs. Rain may keep marketings larger than the past couple of weeks again Thursday, but traders voiced caution in light of recent run up in the lean index. This took much of the premium out of the board. Action in pork bellies also influenced trade, they said.
Rand Financials was a net seller in June and July during the day. Rosenthal Collins sold June late after local short covering provided midday support, pits sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock lightly bought October 80 to 84 calls early and ADM Investor Services bought December 78 calls late, pit sources added.
